name: Bernard Madoff

summary.text: Bernard L. Madoff ran Bernard L. Madoff Investment Securities LLC (BLMIS), through which he operated a Ponzi scheme. On March 12, 2009 he pleaded guilty to all eleven counts of a criminal information, including securities fraud, and on June 29, 2009 Judge Denny Chin sentenced him to 150 years in prison. Recoveries for victims came through the SIPA trustee Irving Picard, who settled with feeder-fund networks including Fairfield Sentry (2010) and Tremont Group ($1.025 billion, 2011), and through the Justice Department's Madoff Victim Fund, whose tenth distribution in December 2024 brought victims to a nearly full recovery. In January 2014 JPMorgan Chase Bank, Madoff's bank, entered a deferred prosecution agreement on two Bank Secrecy Act felony charges and forfeited $1.7 billion.

openQuestions: Site claim that JPMorgan Chase 'settled criminal Bank Secrecy Act charges via a $1.7 billion Deferred Prosecution Agreement without criminal indictments for bank executives': the DPA and $1.7 billion forfeiture are documented; no individual charges were found in the sources returned.

Site claim that JPMorgan 'processed hundreds of billions through Madoff Account 703': the account number and dollar volume were not found in any source returned; the DPA filings on justice.gov should be checked.

Site claim of '$65 billion in paper wealth destroyed': not confirmed; SIPC cites roughly $17.3 billion in principal lost by customers who filed claims, and fictitious account balances are a different measure.

Site claims that feeder funds channeled money 'without due diligence' and that Walter Noel personally profited were not covered by the sources returned, which document the Fairfield Sentry and Tremont settlements only.
The SEC connection is listed from the U.S. Attorney's related-cases page; the SEC's own litigation release against Madoff was not retrieved.
